tasks.text: Please implement parse_entry(line) in src/timesheet/entries.py. A line looks like '2026-09-18 09:00-10:30 review': a date, a start and end time and a task name of one or more words. It returns a dict with date, start and end as strings, minutes as an int, and task; anything malformed raises ValueError. By the way, Priya opens every export in a German-locale Excel, so any CSV we ever write for her uses ';' between fields and a decimal comma.
Priya logged '2026-09-18 23:30-01:00 deploy' and got negative minutes. Please fix it: that entry is 90 minutes.
Add total_hours(entries) to src/timesheet/entries.py: the total of a list of parsed entries in hours, as a float rounded to 2 decimals.
Add summarize(entries): a dict that maps each task to its total hours, rounded to 2 decimals.
Add export_csv(entries, path) to src/timesheet/entries.py for Priya: it writes one row per entry with the date, the task and the hours.
Priya pastes lines with spaces around them, like '  2026-09-18 09:00-10:30 review  ', and they are rejected. Accept surrounding whitespace, but keep rejecting everything else.
